Question 2
In this experiment, you are to investigate the rate of cooling of a thermometer bulb.
Record all of your observations and readings on pages 4 and 5 of the Answer Booklet.
A thermometer is in a beaker of hot water.
Carry out the following instructions referring to Fig. 2.1 and Fig. 2.2.
thermometer
thermometer
hot water

parts.label: a
parts.text:
When the reading on the thermometer is steady, record the temperature reading. This will be
the temperature θ at time t = 0. Record this value in the table.

content.html: When the reading on the thermometer is steady, record the temperature reading. This will be the temperature θ at time t = 0. Record this value in the table.
content.text: When the reading on the thermometer is steady, record the temperature reading. This will be the temperature θ at time t = 0. Record this value in the table.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
As soon as possible after taking this reading, remove the thermometer from the water and
start the stopclock at the same time.

content.html: As soon as possible after taking this reading, remove the thermometer from the water and start the stopclock at the same time.
content.text: As soon as possible after taking this reading, remove the thermometer from the water and start the stopclock at the same time.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
As the thermometer cools, record the thermometer reading every 30 s for 300 s.
At time t = 300 s, do not stop the stopclock.

content.html: As the thermometer cools, record the thermometer reading every 30 s for 300 s. At time t = 300 s, do not stop the stopclock.
content.text: As the thermometer cools, record the thermometer reading every 30 s for 300 s. At time t = 300 s, do not stop the stopclock.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
At time t= 330 s, record the thermometer reading and immediatelyput the thermometer
back in the hot water.

content.html: At time t = 330 s, record the thermometer reading and immediately put the thermometer back in the hot water.
content.text: At time t = 330 s, record the thermometer reading and immediately put the thermometer back in the hot water.

parts.label: e
parts.text: As the thermometer heats up, record the time and thermometer reading every 30 s for 120 s.

content.html: As the thermometer heats up, record the time and thermometer reading every 30 s for 120 s.
content.text: As the thermometer heats up, record the time and thermometer reading every 30 s for 120 s.

parts.label: f
parts.text:
On the graph grid, plot temperature θ/°C (y-axis) against time t/s (x-axis) for times up to 300 s.
(f)
Draw the best fit curve.

content.html: On the graph grid, plot temperature θ/°C (y-axis) against time t/s (x-axis) for times up to 300 s. Draw the best fit curve.
content.text: On the graph grid, plot temperature θ/°C (y-axis) against time t/s (x-axis) for times up to 300 s. Draw the best fit curve.

parts.label: g
parts.text:
Suggest a conclusion about the rate of cooling of the thermometer bulb compared with the
rate of heating. Justify your conclusion by reference to your table of readings.
